extraction.name: RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction
extraction.description: A large-scale and diverse dataset for question-answering on robot failure videos, comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. The dataset includes six types of failures organized across three hierarchical levels of error.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Lu, W., Ye, M., Ye, Z., Tao, R., Yang, S., & Zhao, B. (2025). RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv preprint arXiv:2505.12224.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Simulation data was collected in the ManiSkill environment using expert policies and code snippets to generate erroneous trajectories. Real-world data was collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. For each video, a descriptive text was recorded including the substage, failure taxonomy, and error details.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Simulation data from ManiSkill environment with objects from YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Real-world data from SO-100 robotic arm teleoperation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For simulation data, if motion planning failed resulting in trajectories misaligned with textual descriptions, manual data cleaning was performed, retaining approximately 75% of the collected data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual data cleaning was performed on simulation data to remove misaligned trajectories. Successful trajectories were also collected to prevent overfitting to failure patterns.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Raw data was annotated to construct video-based QA samples for eight question types. Reference answers for five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating) were extracted from textual descriptions. For the remaining three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, low-level correction), GPT-4o was used to generate reference answers based on the video and textual description. All GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and model aim to improve robotic failure recovery, enhancing the robustness and safety of Vision-Language-Action models in real-world deployment.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset includes diverse backgrounds and camera viewpoints to enhance visual diversity and generalization. However, it is limited to specific robotic tasks and environments (simulation and real-world with SO-100 arm).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current integration of the model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not seamless. The model was exclusively applied to the VLA model in this work; hierarchical policies may require targeted correction strategies. The success rate in real-world tasks is still subject to improvement due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is used to train the RoboFAC model for robotic failure analysis and correction, and to evaluate multimodal models' capabilities in robotic failure video understanding.
